cards.title: Arrays hold lists
cards.body: An array keeps values in order inside square brackets. `nums[0]` is the first item and `nums.length` is how many there are.

hi.title: Arrays lists rakhte hain
hi.body: Array values ko square brackets ke andar order mein rakhta hai. `nums[0]` pehla item hai aur `nums.length` batata hai kitne items hain.

cards.title: Reading a line of numbers
cards.body: `split(" ")` cuts text at spaces into an array of pieces, and `.map(Number)` turns each piece into a number.

hi.title: Numbers ki ek line padhna
hi.body: `split(" ")` text ko spaces par kaat kar tukdon ka array banata hai, aur `.map(Number)` har tukde ko number bana deta hai.

cards.title: for...of
cards.body: `for (const x of nums)` visits each item of an array in order.

hi.title: for...of
hi.body: `for (const x of nums)` array ke har item par order mein jaata hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print the last item, 15, but prints `undefined`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: Indexes start at 0, so the last one is `nums.length - 1`: `nums[nums.length - 1]`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse aakhri item 15 print karna chahiye, par yeh `undefined` print karta hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: Indexes 0 se shuru hote hain, isliye aakhri `nums.length - 1` hai: `nums[nums.length - 1]`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: `a.length` is 3, so `a[2]` is the last item, 7. Indexes start at 0.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: `a.length` 3 hai, isliye `a[2]` aakhri item hai, 7. Indexes 0 se shuru hote hain.

exercise.prompt: Read whole numbers on one line, separated by spaces, and print their total.
exercise.promptHi: Ek line mein spaces se alag kiye whole numbers padho aur unka total print karo.
exercise.starterCode:
const nums = prompt().split(" ").map(Number);
// print the total of nums
